items.title: Save our streets from yet more advertising | Letter
items.desc: Reasons to refuse planning permission are limited to ‘public safety’ and ‘amenity’, writes James Ward In response to your report ( Rip out ugly clutter to help revive UK high streets, says thinktank, 13 November ) perhaps we could start with the harbinger of high-street decline, the digital advertising screen. You know the ones, the pavement-blocking LED monoliths, with screens on both sides broadcasting six ads per minute to passersby. Even as shops have shuttered, numbers of such ad machines skyrocketed 256% between 2018 and 2025. The ads shown are invariably for global mega-corporations, further driving commerce online, and for unhealthy products such as junk food, alcohol, gambling and vapes (although the latter are to be banned from 1 June 2027).
